window_title: Rate limiting pattern - Redis docs - Google Chrome
summary: Read the Redis documentation on building a rate limiter with INCR and EXPIRE.
ocr_text:
Redis docs
Pattern: Rate limiter
INCR a key per user per second, set EXPIRE on first write
If the counter is above the limit, reject the request
A sliding window needs a sorted set (ZADD, ZREMRANGEBYSCORE)
Note: Lua scripts keep the check and the increment atomic
outcome: Redis INCR plus EXPIRE gives a fixed window; a Lua script keeps it atomic.

window_title: Postgres as a job queue with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED - Google Chrome
summary: Read an article on using Postgres as a job queue with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED instead of a separate broker.
ocr_text:
Postgres as a job queue
Workers claim jobs with SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE state = 'ready' ORDER BY run_at LIMIT 10 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
SKIP LOCKED lets many workers poll the same table without blocking each other
Keep the transaction short; mark the job done in the same transaction
When not to: more than a few thousand jobs per second, or fan-out to many consumers
outcome: SKIP LOCKED lets many workers claim jobs from one table without blocking.

window_title: psycopg2.OperationalError: SSL SYSCALL error: EOF detected - Stack Overflow - Google Chrome
summary: Looked up psycopg2 'SSL SYSCALL error: EOF detected' after idle connections dropped; the fix is TCP keepalives and pool_pre_ping in SQLAlchemy.
ocr_text:
psycopg2.OperationalError: SSL SYSCALL error: EOF detected
Asked 4 years ago
The load balancer closes idle connections after 350 seconds
Answer (212 votes): enable TCP keepalives: keepalives=1, keepalives_idle=30
With SQLAlchemy, set pool_pre_ping=True so dead connections are replaced before use
Also set pool_recycle below the idle timeout
topic: Fixing dropped Postgres connections in the workers
outcome: Idle connections are cut by the load balancer; keepalives plus pool_pre_ping fix it.
next_steps: Set pool_pre_ping and keepalives in the worker config

window_title: Why your p99 matters more than your average - Google Chrome
summary: Read an article about tail latency: why p99 response time matters more than the average for user-facing APIs.
ocr_text:
Why your p99 matters more than your average
A page that calls 20 services sees the slowest one
If each service has a 1% chance of a slow call, most pages hit at least one
Measure p99 and p99.9, not the mean
Hedged requests and timeouts cut the tail
outcome: Tail latency compounds across fan-out; track p99, not the mean.

Impact: 38 minutes of p99 above 2 s on GET /v2/shipments; 0.4% errors

Resolution: rollback to v3.17.2

2. Query count assertion in serializer tests (ENG-912)
3. Alert at p99 > 1 s instead of 2 s (ENG-913)
